title: The Right Type for Each Field
prompt:
Input `type` changes everything: mobile keyboards, validation, semantics. Fill the three gaps: a password field, an email field, and a field for choosing a date of birth (use `type="date"`). Each keeps its existing `id`.

Rules:
- `password` for the secret, `email` for the address, `date` for the birthday.
- Don't touch ids, labels, or anything else.
boilerplate:
<form>
  <label for="pw">Password</label>
  <input id="pw" type="text">

  <label for="mail">Email</label>
  <input id="mail" type="text">

  <label for="dob">Date of birth</label>
  <input id="dob" type="text">
</form>

tests.name: password field hides its characters
tests.hint: Change the pw input's type to "password" — it masks what is typed.

tests.name: email field validates addresses
tests.hint: type="email" on the mail input gives free validation and the right keyboard.

tests.name: date field uses the date picker
tests.hint: type="date" turns the dob input into a real date picker.

tests.name: ids and labels untouched
tests.hint: Only the three type values change; ids stay exactly as they are.
